arxiv-2112-09915.title: On Two Classes of Modules Related to CS Trivial Extensions
arxiv-2112-09915.creator: Farid Kourki
arxiv-2112-09915.description: Abstract † † Mathematics Subject Classification 2020: 16D10, 16D70, 16D80 Key words and phrases: CS-ring; strongly CS module (ring); trivial extension; weakly IN module (ring) All rings considered are commutative. In this article we introduce and study two notions of modules which are stronger than CS modules, namely weakly IN modules and strongly CS modules.

arxiv-2205-01273.title: Few-Shot Musical Source Separation
arxiv-2205-01273.creator: Yu Wang \sthanks This work was performed while interning at Spotify. This work is partially supported by National Science Foundation award 1544753 & 1955357, Daniel Stoller, Rachel M. Bittner, Juan Pablo Bello
arxiv-2205-01273.description: Abstract Deep learning-based approaches to musical source separation are often limited to the instrument classes that the models are trained on and do not generalize to separate unseen instruments. To address this, we propose a few-shot musical source separation paradigm. We condition a generic U-Net source separation model using few audio examples of the target instrument.

arxiv-2208-07645.title: An Efficient Algorithm to the Integrated Shift and Task Scheduling Problem G S R Murthy T R Lalita SQC & OR Unit, Indian Statistical Institute, St.No.8, Habsiguda, Hyderabad 500007, India Corresponding author :G S R Murthy (murthygsr@gmail.com) trlalita@gmail.com
arxiv-2208-07645.description: Abstract This paper deals with operational models for integrated shift and task scheduling problem. Staff scheduling problem is a special case of this with staff requirements as given input to the problem. Both problems become hard to solve when the problems are considered with flexible shifts. Current literature on these problems leaves good scope for potential research.

arxiv-2212-00209.title: Risk-Averse Self-Scheduling of Storage in Decentralized Markets Thanks: Mr. Yurdakul gratefully acknowledges the support of the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research and the Software Campus program under Grant 01IS17052. Mr. Billimoria’s Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Oxford i
arxiv-2212-00209.creator: Ogun Yurdakul 1 2 and Farhad Billimoria 3
arxiv-2212-00209.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ogun Yurdakul 1 2 and Farhad Billimoria 3. Storage is expected to be a critical source of firming in low-carbon grids. A common concern raised from ex-post assessments is that storage resources can fail to respond to strong price signals during times of scarcity. While commonly attributed to forecast error or failures in operations, we posit that this behavior can be explained from the perspective of risk-averse scheduling.

arxiv-2212-09295.title: Unified, User and Task (UUT) Centered Artificial Intelligence for Metaverse Edge Computing
arxiv-2212-09295.creator: Terence Jie Chua, Wenhan Yu, Jun Zhao
arxiv-2212-09295.description: Abstract The Metaverse can be considered the extension of the present-day web, which integrates the physical and virtual worlds, delivering hyper-realistic user experiences. The inception of the Metaverse brings forth many ecosystem services such as content creation, social entertainment, in-world value transfer, intelligent traffic, healthcare. These services are compute-intensive and require computation offloading onto a Metaverse edge computing server (MECS).

arxiv-2301-01193.title: Measuring the diversity of data and metadata in digital libraries
arxiv-2301-01193.creator: Rafael C. Carrasco, Gustavo Candela, Manuel Marco-Such
arxiv-2301-01193.description: Abstract Diversity indices have been traditionally used to capture the biodiversity of ecosystems by measuring the effective number of species or groups of species. In contrast to abundance, which is correlated with the amount of data available, diversity indices provide a more robust indicator on the variability of individuals.

arxiv-2306-16402.title: Guidance on Individualized Treatment Rule Estimation in High Dimensions
arxiv-2306-16402.creator: Philippe Boileau, Ning Leng, Sandrine Dudoit
arxiv-2306-16402.description: Abstract Individualized treatment rules, cornerstones of precision medicine, inform patient treatment decisions with the goal of optimizing patient outcomes. These rules are generally unknown functions of patients’ pre-treatment covariates, meaning they must be estimated from clinical or observational study data.

arxiv-2405-05969.title: Learned harmonic mean estimation of the Bayesian evidence with normalizing flows
arxiv-2405-05969.creator: Alicja Polanska 1⋆, Matthew A. Price 1, Davide Piras 2,3, Alessio Spurio Mancini 4,1, Jason D. McEwen 1,5†
arxiv-2405-05969.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Alicja Polanska 1⋆, Matthew A. Price 1, Davide Piras 2,3, Alessio Spurio Mancini 4,1, Jason D. McEwen 1,5†. We present the learned harmonic mean estimator with normalizing flows – a robust, scalable and flexible estimator of the Bayesian evidence for model comparison. Since the estimator is agnostic to sampling strategy and simply requires posterior samples, it can be applied to compute the evidence using any Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling technique, including saved down MCMC chains, or any variational inference approach.

arxiv-2412-17441.title: Traveling waves in Bistable Reaction-Diffusion Cellular Automata
arxiv-2412-17441.creator: Daniel Špale, Petr Stehlík
arxiv-2412-17441.description: Abstract . We describe various types of traveling fronts of bistable reaction-diffusion cellular automata. These dynamical systems with discrete time, space, and state spaces can be seen as fully discrete versions of widely studied bistable reaction-diffusion equations. We show that moving traveling waves for high diffusion parameters are restricted to slow speeds and their profiles are interestingly not unique.

arxiv-2501-14045.title: Nonreciprocal entanglement in a molecular optomechanical system
arxiv-2501-14045.creator: E. Kongkui Berinyuy, Jia-Xin Peng, A. Sohail, P. Djorwé, A.-H. Abdel-Aty, N. Alessa, K.S. Nisar, S. G. Nana Engo
arxiv-2501-14045.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by E. Kongkui Berinyuy, Jia-Xin Peng, A. Sohail, P. Djorwé, A.-H. Abdel-Aty, N. Alessa, K.S. Nisar, S. G. Nana Engo. We propose a theoretical scheme to generate nonreciprocal bipartite entanglement between a cavity mode and vibrational modes in a molecular cavity optomechanical system. Our system consists of 𝒩 \mathcal{N} molecules placed inside a spinning whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) resonator.

arxiv-2507-14397.title: Efficient LLM Inference: Bandwidth, Compute, Synchronization, and Capacity are all you need
arxiv-2507-14397.creator: Michael Davies, Neal Crago, Karthikeyan Sankaralingam, Christos Kozyrakis
arxiv-2507-14397.description: Abstract This paper presents a limit study of transformer-based large language model (LLM) inference, focusing on the fundamental performance bottlenecks imposed by memory bandwidth, memory capacity, and synchronization overhead in distributed inference systems. We develop a hardware-agnostic performance model that abstracts away implementation details, enabling the analysis of a wide range of current and near-future hardware technologies.

Atmospheric aerosols affect the global energy budget by scattering and absorbing sunlight (direct effects) and by changing the microphysical structure, lifetime, and coverage of clouds (indirect effects). europmc-pmc7916865.creator: Sachdev S, Ansari SA, Ansari MI, Fujita M, Hasanuzzaman M.
europmc-pmc7916865.description: Climate change is an invisible, silent killer with calamitous effects on living organisms. As the sessile organism, plants experience a diverse array of abiotic stresses during ontogenesis. The relentless climatic changes amplify the intensity and duration of stresses, making...

plos-pone-0003166.title: Pedestrian Road Traffic Injuries in Urban Peruvian Children and Adolescents: Case Control Analyses of Personal and Environmental Risk Factors
plos-pone-0003166.creator: Joseph Donroe, Monica Tincopa, Robert H. Gilman et al.
plos-pone-0003166.description: PLOS ONE research article. Child pedestrian road traffic injuries (RTIs) are an important cause of death and disability in poorer nations, however RTI prevention strategies in those countries largely draw upon studies conducted in wealthier countries. This research investigated personal and environmental r

pmc-10580959.title: A prebiotic diet modulates the oral microbiome composition and results in the attenuation of oropharyngeal candidiasis in mice
pmc-10580959.creator: Roberto Vazquez-Munoz, Angela Thompson, Takanori Sobue, Anna Dongari-Bagtzoglou
pmc-10580959.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Oral bacteria can influence the ability of Candida albicans to cause oropharyngeal candidiasis (OPC). We recently reported that a Lactobacillus johnsonii-enriched oral microbiota reduced C. albicans virulence in an immunosuppressed OPC mouse model. As a follow-up, in this work, we aimed to enrich the resident oral Lactobacillus communities with a prebiotic diet to further assess their effect on the severity of OPC. We tested the effect of a prebiotic xylo-oligosaccharides (XOS)-enriched diet in the oral global bacterial composition and severity of OPC.

pmc-11484636.title: ﻿Schiedeawaiahuluensis (Caryophyllaceae), an enigmatic new species from Kaua'i, Hawaiian Islands and the first species discovered by a drone collection system
pmc-11484636.creator: Warren L. Wagner, Stephen G. Weller, Ann K. Sakai, Ben Nyberg, Kenneth R. Wood
pmc-11484636.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ﻿AbstractDuring a survey by the National Tropical Botanical Garden drone team, an enigmatic Schiedea was observed in December 2021on steep, rocky cliff faces of the Waiahulu Valley in the Waimea Canyon of Kaua'i. Subsequently, another survey was conducted in March 2022 and, by use of a remotely controlled cutting device suspended below the drone, the first herbarium specimen was collected, as well as a seed collection of an undescribed cliff-dwelling species of Schiedea.

pmc-11591417.title: Isavuconazole and Amphotericin B Synergic Antifungal Activity: In Vitro Evaluation on Pulmonary Aspergillosis Molds Isolates
pmc-11591417.creator: Maddalena Calvo, Flavio Lauricella, Anna Maurizia Mellini, Guido Scalia, Laura Trovato
pmc-11591417.description: Background/Objectives. Pulmonary aspergillosis is a severe respiratory infection caused by Aspergillus spp., whose resistance profiles and invasive attitude complicate therapeutical strategies. Several aspergillosis cases emerged as superinfections during the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic when isavuconazole and amphotericin B became essential antifungal alternatives. The main purpose of the present study was to investigate a possible synergic activity between these molecules against Aspergillus spp.

pmc-12358503.title: A multilevel analysis on spatiotemporal and individual-level determinants of tuberculosis treatment failure in China
pmc-12358503.creator: Chunping Huang, Yifei Wu, Qinglin Cheng, Qingchun Li, Ming Lu, Lei Zhang
pmc-12358503.description: By exploring the factors that influence treatment failure in tuberculosis, the study aimed to provide references for the treatment and management of tuberculosis. The study data were derived from the National Tuberculosis Specialized Reporting System. Univariate analysis was used to test individual characteristic variables related to tuberculosis treatment failure.

pmc-12504694.title: Behavioral shifts of reintroduced Milu deer Elaphurus davidianus in East Dongting lake of China
pmc-12504694.creator: Zhibin Cheng, Hong Zhang, Jialiang Ma, Chengmiao Feng, Wei Liu, Zhenyu Zhong, Qingyun Guo, Qingxun Zhang, Pan Zhang, Shumiao Zhang, Cheng Zong, Jiade Bai, Kun Cheng
pmc-12504694.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Reintroduction is an important method for recovering endangered and rare species in their natural habitats. Understanding how these species adapt to new environments is essential for their conservation and population recovery. However, behavioral adaption (particularly circadian activity patterns) of reintroduced Milu deer (Elaphurus davidianus), a special species disappeared in the wild for centuries, remains poorly understood during their initial release into historical range from captivity.

pmc-12569633.title: Gas-phase synthesis of naphthalene through an unconventional thermal alkyne–alkene [2 + 2] cycloaddition mechanism
pmc-12569633.creator: Shane J. Goettl, Iakov A. Medvedkov, Anatoliy A. Nikolayev, Chao He, Zhenghai Yang, Alexander M. Mebel, Ankit Somani, Adrian Portela-Gonzalez, Wolfram Sander, Ralf I. Kaiser
pmc-12569633.description: Exotic cycloaddition entrance channels were discovered for the bimolecular gas-phase reactions of the phenylethynyl radical (C6H5CC, X2A1) with ethylene-d4 (C2D4) and propylene (C3H6) as explored under single-collision conditions utilizing the crossed molecular beams technique combined with electronic structure and statistical calculations.

pmc-12589055.title: Exploring health needs and the double burden of disease in adults attending public health facilities in the Iraqi Kurdistan
pmc-12589055.creator: Stefania Moramarco, Mariagrazia Cicala, Faiq B. Basa, Gorgees S. Akhshirsh, Antonia Bezenchek, Rafal S. L. Adhama, Bayar S. Azeez, Sivar A. Qadir, Shahla O. Salih, Luma H. H. Alhanabadi, Iuri Fanti, Berivan A. Tofiq, Daniele Di Giovanni, Leonardo Emberti Gialloreti, Paola Scarcella
pmc-12589055.description: ObjectiveWe analyzed the health needs of the adult population accessing public health facilities in the Iraqi Kurdistan, a region facing both demographic and epidemiological transitions while undergoing post-crisis recovery. We investigates the prevalence and distribution of communicable and non-communicable diseases using real-world data from a digital surveillance system.

pmc-12655389.title: Influence of Calcination Temperature on the Structure and Antimicrobial Properties of Arthrospira platensis-Mediated Zinc Oxide Nanoparticles
pmc-12655389.creator: Noor Akhras, Abuzer Çelekli, Hüseyin Bozkurt, Hwankyu Lee
pmc-12655389.description: Background/Objectives: Arthrospira platensis (A. platensis) is a cyanobacterium rich in bioactive compounds with proven antioxidant, antimicrobial, and stabilizing properties, making it an ideal candidate for the green synthesis of zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs). This study aimed to synthesize ZnO NPs using A. platensis extract and to evaluate the influence of post-synthesis temperature on their physicochemical and antimicrobial properties.

pmc-12993702.title: Incidence of Adverse Events in Peripheral Intravenous Vasopressor Use
pmc-12993702.creator: Shang-Jun ZhangJian, Kuang-Yu Niu, Chen-Bin Chen, Chen-June Seak, Chieh-Ching Yen
pmc-12993702.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines incidence of adverse events and central venous catheter avoidance after peripheral intravenous administration of vasopressors in adults with hypotension, shock, or critical illness. Introduction Shock is defined as inadequate cellular oxygen utilization, resulting in tissue hypoperfusion that, if not promptly identified and treated, can lead to significant morbidity and mortality.

pmc-13267569.creator: Takuma Kurachi, Tsuyoshi Shimmura

pmc-13470004.title: Social processing in the amygdala: single-nucleus RNA-sequencing reveals distinct neuronal responses to dominant and subordinate cues
pmc-13470004.creator: Madeleine F. Dwortz, Hans A. Hofmann, James P. Curley
pmc-13470004.description: The amygdala serves as a critical neural hub for interpreting social cues, with its distinct subregions and diverse neuronal populations playing specialized roles in processing these signals. Here, we employ single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) to characterize neuronal responses in the mouse amygdala to olfactory cues associated with social dominance, uncovering distinct activation patterns within glutamatergic and GABAergic populations.

pmc-13482290.title: Suicidal ideation as an additional risk for violence against women residing in shelters: a clinical sample analysis in Hong Kong
pmc-13482290.creator: Ko Ling Chan, Qianru Wu, Qiqi Chen
pmc-13482290.description: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a major public health issue associated with adverse mental health outcomes, including suicidal ideation. However, limited research has examined the correlates of suicidal ideation among shelter-seeking women. This study analyzed data from a clinical sample of 597 women who sought services from three major shelters for battered women in Hong Kong between 2020 and 2024.

pmc-13688728.title: Factors associated with preventive behaviors for microvascular complications and self-reported neuropathy symptoms among community-dwelling individuals with type 2 diabetes in Thailand
pmc-13688728.creator: Nanda Win, Natthida Phoosuwan, Junjira Phasom, Pakorn Pusuwan, Sandeep Poddar, Pankaew Tantirattanakulchai, Nitikorn Phoosuwan
pmc-13688728.description: BackgroundType 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a significant public health issue globally, with a high burden of microvascular complications, including diabetic retinopathy, nephropathy, and neuropathy. Preventive behaviors play a critical role in reducing the risk and progression of these complications; however, the factors influencing such behaviors remain insufficiently understood.
